metadata.title: Agentic AI Emergence — 2026
metadata.description: Focused view on how AI and agentic AI change the generic vulnerabilities across the TLCTC clusters. This is a narrow snapshot — it intentionally leaves other tech types empty so the agentic-specific story stands out. Use it as a starting frame for agentic-AI threat discussions with leadership, red teams, or architecture boards.
metadata.author: TLCTC community (curated)

instances.notes: Commodity floor for the agentic-AI threat stack: before agents plan and act, basic generative AI has already lowered the cost of convincing phishing content across email, voice, and video. Included here to anchor the maturity curve.

Threat actors use LLMs to write loaders, refactor existing malware, and automate obfuscation. Microsoft/OpenAI have publicly disclosed state-actor model abuse. This is the step before agents write and deploy their own tooling end-to-end.

references.title: Microsoft — Staying ahead of threat actors in the age of AI

instances.notes: Face-swap and synthetic video toolkits bypass remote identity verification. Established criminal tradecraft at banks, exchanges, and lenders. Sets the stage for agent chains that stitch identity bypass into end-to-end fraud flows.

Indirect prompt injection exfiltrates context or triggers unintended actions on customer-facing assistants. Classified #1 Abuse of Functions — the LLM input channel is used as designed, just with adversarial content.

Agents wired to browser, shell, email, or file-system tools can be coerced via indirect prompt injection to perform unintended tool calls. This is the most urgent agentic-AI-specific risk: the agent's own tool-use channel becomes the generic vulnerability.
Experimental agents run multi-turn chat with victims over Telegram/WhatsApp, adapting persona and pressure dynamically. A force multiplier for existing criminal call-center operations.

Research agents chain recon → vulnerability discovery → exploitation autonomously (HackingBuddyGPT, XBOW). Dual-use: defensive red-team tooling already being forked offensively. First-mover maturity — demonstrated against real targets, not yet mass-deployed.

Agents scan ecosystems for typo-squat opportunities, auto-generate malicious packages, and publish at a rate outpacing human defenders. Early indicators in Shai-Hulud and Chalk/Debug incidents where tooling looked agent-assisted.

Agents chain infostealer output directly into authentication flows across harvested services. The Axiom-X credential duality collapses into one automated pipeline: acquire, authenticate, exfiltrate, monetize — in minutes.

Hypothetical: malware whose C2 is an embedded agent that rewrites its own code in response to the target environment. Not seen in the wild — classical polymorphism is not this. Watch item for state actors with frontier-model access.
